title: Sense-Think-Act Clock Sorter
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Clocks and Watches with AI
description: Drag eight clock parts into Sensors, Microcontroller, and Actuators columns, get a hint for every wrong drop, then step one signal through the sense-think-act loop.

educational.topic: Sensors, microcontrollers, and actuators in a clock
learningObjectives: Classify clock parts as sensors, a microcontroller, or actuators.
Explain the direction information flows between each part and the Pico.
Describe one full sense-think-act cycle in an auto-dimming clock.
prerequisites: Read the Sensors and Actuators section of Chapter 1.

accessibility.notes: Screen-reader description provided; all controls are standard HTML elements.

controls.label: Part cards
controls.description: Drag each card into a column; correct drops snap in place, wrong drops return with a hint.

controls.label: Reset
controls.description: Returns all cards to the tray in a new order.

controls.label: Next step
controls.description: Enabled after all cards are placed; steps a signal from sensor to Pico to display.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Classification with immediate feedback, followed by a worked example
keyQuestions: Does information flow toward the Pico or away from it for this part?
Why is a real-time clock chip an input even though it "keeps time"?
Which part does the "think" step in every clock?
commonMisconceptions: Calling a display an input because it "shows information." It only receives data from the Pico.
Calling the real-time clock an actuator because it "does something." It reports the time to the Pico, so it is an input.
Thinking the Pico is a sensor because it has pins that read signals. The pins belong to the controller that runs the program.
assessmentOpportunities: Students sort all eight parts with no more than one hint.
Students can explain, using the words "to the Pico" or "from the Pico," why each part is a sensor or an actuator.
Students can describe a sense-think-act cycle for a clock feature not shown in the MicroSim.
